title: Rav Gidel bar Menashya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: We find in Moed Katan 24a: "Rav Gidel bar Menashya said in the name of Shmuel," and there, 24b: "Rav Gidel bar Menashya said in the name of Rav," and in Bava Batra 155b: "Gidel bar Menashya sent to Rav (so is the reading of the Rashbam), 'Let our master teach us,'" but the reading of the Rif and the Rosh, and so is the reading of the Gemara, is that he sent to Rava. Hyman concludes that of necessity one must say that there were two: Rav Gidel bar Menashya was a student of Rav and Shmuel, and so it is proven from Pesachim 107a that he was of the generation of simply Rav Gidel; but Gidel bar Menashya was a student of Rava. In Dikdukei Soferim the reading "Gadol bar Menashi" or "bar Menashe" is brought, and so too the reading before Sefer Yuchasin was "bar Menashi." It is very close to say that he is Rav Gidel bar Menashe of Biri of Narash, mentioned in Yoma 81b, who expounded: "The halakha does not follow Rabbi"; everyone went out, diluted vinegar and drank it; he heard and became angry.

notes.text: Hyman distinguishes an earlier student of Rav and Shmuel from a later Gidel associated with Rava; Rav/Rava and Menashi/Menashe are transmitted variants. The Yoma vinegar account says they diluted it and drank it.

The consulted Bava Batra 155b text reads Rava, while Rashbam there explicitly explains the exchange with Rav. Yoma 81b says that they diluted and drank vinegar, followed by Gidel’s objection about first-instance permission, quantity and dilution. Hyman’s two-person conclusion and proposed Biri-of-Narash identification remain his argument; the exact Rif, Rosh, Dikdukei Soferim and Yuchasin editions were not independently inspected.
